title: Housekeeping stream cleanup is neither guaranteed nor verified
test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'a test stream whose status request fails mid-run is stopped before the setup fails (VAL-116)', 'a test stream that cannot be confirmed stopped ends the setup before the video or encoder changes (VAL-116)', 'a deadline that passes while the test stream runs stops it before the rollback restores anything (VAL-116)', 'a test stream OBS refuses to start is still stopped and seen idle before the video changes (VAL-116)', 'a stop held for a stream started outside the transaction is rolled back only while it is held'; guards that passed before and after: 'a stop OBS refuses for a test stream that is already down is not a failure (VAL-116)', 'a setup that fails after a clean test stream does not stop the stream again in its rollback'; changed: 'setup work still running when the deadline passes sends nothing while the rollback runs'
proof: Holds. releaseStaleEncoder sent StartStream, polled, then StopStream with no try/finally, ignored the StopStream answer, and after 40 status polls returned true whenever the stream had been seen running, active or not; configureObsStream then went on to SetVideoSettings and the encoder profile writes. Nothing journaled the raw test stream, so a rollback (also the deadline's, added by TASK-080) left it running. The tests drive configureObsStream against fake OBS sockets that log every request. On the unchanged code: a status poll that timed out after StartStream ended the setup with the log '..., StartStream, GetStreamStatus, SetStreamServiceSettings' and no StopStream ('the StartStream at 3 is not stopped'); with OBS refusing the stop, or accepting it while the output stayed up, the setup sent SetVideoSettings (and the encoder writes) after about 4 s of polling ('SetVideoSettings sent while the test stream may still run', true !== false); a deadline between the test stream's start and its first poll restored the service and closed with the stream still running (log missing 'StopStream', 'GetStreamStatus' before the restore); a StartStream OBS refused was followed by no stop at all. Fix: each run is wrapped in try/finally; the finally sends StopStream and polls fail-closed (only outputActive === false and not reconnecting counts as down; a request that fails ends the check unconfirmed), also after a failed request or a refused start, and the request error is rethrown after the cleanup. releaseStaleEncoder returns { released, stopped, message }, and configureObsStream ends the setup through finish when stopped is false, before any video or encoder change ('OBS could not confirm that the short test stream ... stopped (StopStream: output busy; output still active after 4000ms), so setup ended before changing the video or encoder settings.'). A new transaction.hold(step) journals a StopStream only while a test stream may be running and drops it once the stop is confirmed, so a rollback that begins meanwhile (the deadline, when housekeeping is refused) or after an unconfirmed stop stops the stream and passes the stop gate before restoring anything; after a clean reset nothing is journaled (guard test: one StopStream only). Mutation checks: removing the finally, ignoring stopped, removing the hold, releasing the hold after an unconfirmed stop, or skipping the stop after a refused start each fail at least one of the new tests. node --test tests/obsWebSocket.test.js tests/obsWebSocketWire.test.js 60/60, npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (1059/1059) pass.

title: Configuration broadcasts even when autoStart is false
test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'without auto-start an idle OBS still runs the encoder-reset test stream once, and stops it (section-84098610a3c7f7be0c63f39f/Q-001, VAL-117)' (pins the decided behaviour; passed before and after)
proof: Holds, and left to TASK-096 by the owner's answer 3 (dev-notes/answers.md): the reset is kept when autoStart is false, on the condition that its test stream goes to a probe target the server never forwards to viewers, and TASK-096 owns that change; TASK-082 does not gate the reset on autoStart. With OBS idle and autoStart false, configureObsStream still points OBS at the room's WHIP URL and runs the short test stream there, so until TASK-096 lands it does broadcast briefly to the room. Recorded the decision in a code comment at the reset in configureObsStream (citing section-84098610a3c7f7be0c63f39f/Q-001) and in the VAL-117 test: with autoStart false exactly one StartStream is sent, it is followed by a StopStream and an idle status before SetVideoSettings, no start follows, the output is inactive at the end and the message still asks to click Start Streaming in OBS. No test can fail on the unchanged code for this issue within this item, since the behaviour it reports is the one the owner chose to keep here.
